Egyptian lubricants company that blends and sells motor oils, industrial oils, greases and related petroleum products, serving car owners, transport fleets, factories and the oil and gas sector. It earns revenue from wholesale and retail distribution of its branded lubricants across Egypt, with some export activity, and has been investing in expanding production capacity. Based in Cairo and linked to the Egyptian state-owned petroleum sector, it is a regional industrial player. Brand visibility is moderate: known to Egyptian motorists and garages, but little recognition outside the Middle East and North Africa.

Oak Row Equities is a vertically integrated real estate private equity firm based in New York. It operates in the property development and investment space, combining in-house sourcing, development and management of real estate assets rather than relying only on outside partners. Investors and capital partners fund its projects, and it earns returns from the acquisition, development and sale or operation of properties. It has raised a substantial amount of capital in recent years. Public detail on its portfolio and team is limited, so it appears to be a B2B and investor-facing firm without consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Indian hospitality technology company behind the OYO brand, which franchises and leases budget and mid-range hotels, homes and vacation rentals. Owners list rooms on the OYO platform, which provides branding, pricing, booking and operational support; OYO earns commissions and fees. The Singapore entity is the group's overseas holding arm, while the operating business is led from Gurugram, India. Founded in 2013 by Ritesh Agarwal, it has operated across India, Southeast Asia, Europe, the US and the Middle East, and was backed heavily by SoftBank. The group has pursued an Indian IPO. High consumer brand visibility in India and Asia, sold mostly through its app.

Technology skills and learning platform for software developers, IT professionals and creative staff, offering video courses, skill assessments, hands-on labs and analytics for managers. It sells subscriptions to enterprises and individuals, with customers including large corporations and government bodies that train technical staff. Founded in 2004 in Utah and headquartered in Westlake Village, California, it went public on Nasdaq in 2018 and was taken private by Vista Equity Partners in 2021. It acquired GitPrime, Smarterer and others, and bought A Cloud Guru in 2021. Moderate brand awareness among technologists and IT buyers; largely B2B.

Africa's largest food retailer, operating supermarkets and hypermarkets under Shoprite, Checkers, Checkers Hyper, Usave and OK Furniture banners, plus liquor, pharmacy and convenience formats. It sells groceries, fresh food and household goods mainly to mass-market and middle-income shoppers in South Africa and, historically, other African countries, and also runs the Xtra Savings loyalty programme and money-transfer services. Headquartered in Brackenfell near Cape Town, it is listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (SHP) and has well over 2,800 outlets and around 150,000 staff. Very high consumer brand visibility across Southern Africa.

Twenty-four-hour, key-card access fitness club franchisor offering gyms with cardio and weights equipment, group classes and personal training for everyday members. Founded in 2003 in Minnesota, it franchises clubs around the world, earning franchise fees, royalties and member-related revenue, with several hundred locations across multiple countries. Headquartered in Chanhassen, Minnesota, it has been part of the Lift Brands group and is run as a smaller, more value-oriented alternative to larger gym chains. Established consumer fitness brand with solid local presence, though less global recognition than the largest gym names.

Infrastructure and civil construction contractor that builds and rehabilitates bridges, dams, tunnels, marine facilities, pipelines, power plants and other heavy projects across the US, Canada and offshore. Customers are mainly public agencies and utilities, with revenue from large long-term construction contracts. Headquartered in Grapevine, Texas, it combines the legacy of Johnson Brothers and Southland Contracting, and became publicly listed on NYSE American (SLND) in 2023 through a SPAC merger with Legato Merger Corp. II. Strongly B2B, with little consumer awareness, though well known in infrastructure and civil engineering circles.

Cleantech company developing an electrochemical process to produce cement without the carbon emissions of traditional kilns, aimed at cutting the large global carbon footprint of cement production. Its technology, spun out of MIT and founded in 2019, makes low-carbon cement at ambient temperatures using electricity and sells to construction firms and concrete producers. Based in Somerville, Massachusetts, it has built a pilot plant in Massachusetts and a commercial-scale factory in Holyoke, with backing from Breakthrough Energy Ventures and the US Department of Energy. Offtake agreements with companies like Microsoft have been announced. B2B, with visibility mainly in climate-tech circles.

Technology company based in Sunnyvale, California, developing energy-efficient AI inference chips and systems for running large models in data centers; it was previously known as Recogni and rebranded as Tensordyne. It aims to sell hardware and software to cloud providers and enterprises building out AI capacity, where power consumption is the main constraint. Customers would be hyperscalers and data-center operators, so it is a B2B deep-tech company with minimal consumer brand awareness and a young public profile under its new name.

Private real estate investment and development firm founded by Joseph Sitt in 1986 in New York, owning and managing retail, hotel and commercial properties. It is known for high-street retail holdings on Fifth Avenue, Times Square, Chicago's Magnificent Mile, Beverly Hills and Miami, plus Coney Island amusement-area developments and a portfolio of hotels. Revenue comes from rents, property sales and development. It has held billions of dollars of assets and invests in the US and Europe. Privately owned and B2B; visible to retailers and brands through its flagship locations, but low direct consumer awareness.

Hong Kong-based digital payments and fintech group best known for TNG Wallet, a mobile e-wallet for Hong Kong users, together with cross-border remittance and payment services. It was founded in 2013 and is backed by Ant Group, which owns a stake and shares technology with related wallets in the region. Customers are consumers, migrant workers and merchants, earning revenue from remittance fees, payment processing and financial services. It also works with partners in Southeast Asia. Moderate consumer brand awareness in Hong Kong, mostly via its app and merchant acceptance.

Private, non-profit research university founded in 1890 and based in Chicago's Hyde Park neighbourhood. It enrolls roughly 17,000 students across the College, graduate programmes, Booth School of Business, Pritzker School of Law and Pritzker School of Medicine, and runs the University of Chicago Medical Center, the University of Chicago Press and associated laboratories such as Argonne and Fermilab. Income comes from tuition, research grants, philanthropy, an endowment worth around ten billion dollars and clinical activity. It has produced many Nobel laureates. Widely recognised academic brand, though it is not a consumer-product company.

Saudi Arabian real estate company headquartered in Riyadh, involved in developing, owning and managing residential, commercial and mixed-use projects. Its revenue comes from property sales, leasing and asset management, serving Saudi homebuyers, investors and tenants. It is listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul) and is among the established Saudi property names, helped by the Kingdom's housing and urban development push under Vision 2030. Its brand is known mainly within Saudi Arabia's real estate community and has limited recognition outside the Gulf region.

ATAA Educational Co is an educational company based in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Crunchbase tags place it in education and higher education. It most likely provides private education or training services to students in the Kingdom, but the data given does not name its schools, programmes, owners or size. As a Saudi regional operator it probably has local rather than international brand awareness, with customers being students and families. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Specialist lender providing discreet asset-backed loans secured against luxury items such as jewellery, watches, fine art, cars and other high-value possessions, for affluent clients who need short-term liquidity without selling the asset. Originally a UK brand founded in 2006 in London, Borro also operated in the United States, earning interest and fees on loans and income from selling forfeited items. Customers are high-net-worth individuals, collectors and small business owners. Niche, discreet brand with limited public profile, mostly known in the luxury lending and auction community.

Healthcare navigation and benefits platform used by employers and health plans to help employees compare providers, understand costs and use their benefits. Its software combined price transparency, personalised guidance and wellbeing tools, and it sold subscriptions to large employers and insurers. Founded in 2008 in San Francisco and later headquartered in Utah, it went public on the NYSE in 2014 (CSLT). It was acquired by Vera Whole Health in 2022 for around 370 million dollars, combining navigation with on-site primary care. Customers included many Fortune 500 firms. B2B with little consumer awareness.

One of Sri Lanka's largest private commercial banks, offering retail, corporate, SME, trade finance, treasury, leasing and digital banking services through a nationwide branch and ATM network. It also operates overseas in Bangladesh and the Maldives through subsidiaries and branches. Founded in 1969 and headquartered in Colombo, it is listed on the Colombo Stock Exchange (COMB) and is regularly ranked among the top banks in the country, with many billions of rupees in assets. Consumer-facing brand with very high awareness in Sri Lanka, though little profile abroad.

FIBRAeMX is a Mexican investment vehicle based in Mexico City (Miguel Hidalgo), classified by Crunchbase under hedge funds. Its short description says it focuses on a road network and a company portfolio, which suggests an asset-backed trust holding road infrastructure and related business interests in Mexico. Nothing further, such as size, sponsors or listing details, is available in the data provided. It is an investor-facing vehicle and would have no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Chinese live-streaming social app launched in the mid-2010s, where broadcasters perform and chat with viewers who send virtual gifts bought with real money, which form the main revenue source. It was developed by Beijing-based Huajiao and later acquired by Qihoo 360 Technology. Users are mostly young Chinese mobile consumers, with popular streamers earning from gifts. It is part of the competitive Chinese streaming sector alongside YY and Douyin. Consumer app with mass-market recognition within China, nearly none abroad.

German online retailer specialising in lamps, lighting and lighting accessories, selling through its own web shop and marketplaces across many European countries under country-specific domains such as lampenwelt.de, lampenwelt.at and other regional shops. It offers a catalogue of tens of thousands of products from decorative pendant lights to LED lamps and smart-home lighting, and earns revenue from online sales to consumers and some trade customers. Founded in 2000 and based in Fulda, Hesse, it has been owned by the Lampenwelt Group and also operates the Lampe.de and Lumicom brands. Strong niche consumer visibility in German-speaking markets.

London-based AI cloud infrastructure provider, offering GPU compute to train, serve and scale AI models, with a software platform around it. Founded in 2018 as Ori Industries, it sells to AI start-ups, enterprises and telecom operators that need dedicated GPU capacity or private AI clouds, with partners in Europe and the Middle East. Revenue comes from GPU capacity rental and platform fees. It has raised substantial venture funding and competes with specialist GPU clouds such as CoreWeave and Lambda. B2B, with limited public recognition outside the AI and cloud community.

Panepinto Properties is a real estate development company based in Jersey City, New Jersey. The Crunchbase description and industry tag identify it as a property developer, which suggests it builds, owns and manages residential and commercial real estate projects in the New Jersey and New York metropolitan area. Detail on its projects, size and staff is not available in the data given. As a local developer it is likely to have little consumer brand profile beyond its immediate market, and customers would be tenants, buyers and investors. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Direct-to-consumer oral care brand known for its electric toothbrush with a sleek metal handle, sold with subscription refill brush heads and toothpaste. Founded in 2014 in Brooklyn, New York, it sells online and through retailers such as Target and Walmart, with revenue from recurring replacement subscriptions and device purchases. Quip also offers mouthwash, floss and dental advice, and has raised funding from backers including Founders Fund. It targets mainstream consumers and is among the better known challenger oral care brands in the United States.

New York-based invention platform founded in 2009 by Ben Kaufman that turned crowd-sourced product ideas into consumer goods, selling through retailers like Target and Bed Bath & Beyond. Community members submitted and voted on ideas, and Quirky handled design, engineering, manufacturing and marketing, paying inventors a share of revenue. It partnered with GE for the Wink smart home line. After heavy spending it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in 2015, and its assets, including Wink, were sold. Had some consumer visibility through retail shelves, now largely defunct as a business.

South Korean logistics company running dawn delivery and fulfilment for e-commerce, specialising in temperature-controlled and fresh-food freight. It operates a network of trucks, warehouses and a software platform that serves online sellers, retailers and shippers, with revenue from delivery fees and logistics services. Based in Seoul, it was founded in the late 2010s and received venture funding for its cold-chain network and for expansion into broader logistics. It is a B2B service known mainly among Korean e-commerce merchants rather than ordinary consumers.

Pakistani microfinance bank providing digital financial services, mobile accounts, remittances and small loans, best known for its Easypaisa mobile wallet brand, which was launched with Telenor Pakistan in 2009. Based in Karachi, it was owned by Telenor Group and Ant Group, which took a stake in 2018, and Telenor's majority stake was sold to Ant Group's affiliate in 2023 as Telenor exited Pakistan. It has tens of millions of customers using Easypaisa for bill payments, transfers and savings. Very strong consumer brand awareness in Pakistan.

British flooring manufacturer and distributor producing carpets, rugs, underlay, vinyl, LVT, ceramic tiles and laminate, sold to consumers, retailers and contractors across the UK, Europe and Australia. Based in Kidderminster, Worcestershire, the home of English carpet making, it operates under brands such as Cormar, Abingdon, Westex, Ulster Carpets and Cavalier. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (VCP), the group generates about 1 billion pounds in annual sales and has bought up several brands. Strong trade brand in UK flooring but not a mass consumer name.

Chinese manufacturer of rail transit equipment and high-performance materials such as rubber and plastic products for rail, wind and construction use, belonging to the CRRC group. Zhuzhou Times New Material Technology is listed in Shanghai (600458) and makes products such as railway track fittings, rubber springs, polymer composites, thin-film capacitors and material for new energy vehicles, selling mainly to China's rail operators and industrial firms. Based in Zhuzhou, Hunan, it is a state-linked supplier within the CRRC ecosystem. B2B only, with essentially no consumer brand awareness.

UK rural broadband provider using a mix of fixed wireless and full-fibre networks to deliver high-speed internet to homes and businesses in areas that larger operators neglect. Based in Droitwich, Worcestershire, it covers parts of England and Wales and has built fibre networks with local authority subsidies, such as through the Gigabit Voucher Scheme and Project Gigabit contracts. Revenue comes from monthly subscriptions and government-funded builds. Backed by funds such as Aviva Investors, it has been growing quickly. Regional consumer brand with strong awareness in its served rural communities.

Sports and marketing arm of Alibaba Group, set up in 2015 as a platform integrating sport events, media rights, marketing and fan services in China. Alisports ran projects from event operation and ticketing to football and esports properties, and worked with sports bodies, clubs and rights holders on digital content. It became part of Alibaba's digital media and entertainment unit and sells sponsorship, rights and data-driven marketing to brands. It is based in Shanghai and widely known within the Chinese sports industry, with little recognition abroad. Directly relevant to sports sponsorship as an intermediary.

British infrastructure and engineering group working in transport, water, energy and defence, with technology and consulting services for road, rail and nuclear schemes. Customers are mainly government agencies and regulated utilities such as National Highways, Network Rail and water companies. Founded in 1865 and headquartered in London, it is listed on the London Stock Exchange (COST) and employs thousands of people, with revenue of around 1.2 billion pounds. Known for projects such as the Thames Barrier-adjacent works and Lower Thames Crossing involvement. B2B, with solid industry reputation but low consumer awareness.

Large Indian real estate developer founded in 1993 and based in Bengaluru, building office parks, residential communities, hotels and retail space. Embassy Group developed landmark business parks such as Embassy Manyata and Embassy Golf Links, and has a large commercial portfolio of tens of millions of square feet, much of it held through the listed Embassy Office Parks REIT, which launched in 2019 as India's first REIT. Tenants include multinational technology firms. Privately held by the Embassy family and partners such as Blackstone. Well known in Indian real estate, with a premium residential brand.

Transportation management platform that helps freight brokers and shippers manage truckload shipments, with software for load planning, carrier communication, visibility and invoicing. It sells subscriptions to logistics companies and shippers and was based in Scottsdale, Arizona. Emerge was acquired by Echo Global Logistics and its software became part of Echo's platform in the late 2010s. B2B and mostly unknown to the public, with value limited to logistics and supply chain customers.

First Fix is a company based in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, described as a local market dealer that delivers high-quality construction products. Its Crunchbase tags place it in construction and project management. It most likely sells building materials and supplies or contractor services to builders and developers in the Saudi market. Further detail on products, customers and scale is not available. The brand appears to have regional B2B visibility only. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Materials technology company producing low-carbon cement alternatives by processing waste or captured emissions into supplementary cementitious materials, notably its Rock Cement and reactive calcium silicate hydrate products that reduce the CO2 emissions of concrete. Based in San Jose, California, it works with cement and concrete producers, and has built a plant in Redding, California, with investors including Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund, Cemex Ventures and Microsoft. B2B and aimed at construction materials producers, with low consumer awareness but growing visibility within the climate-tech and building materials communities.

Brazilian online lender offering fast, fully digital personal loans to individuals who struggle to access traditional bank credit, using data and credit models for approval. Founded in 2012 in Sao Paulo, it earns interest and fees on loans funded by institutional partners. It has served hundreds of thousands of customers, positions itself as a fairer alternative to high-cost credit, and has received venture funding from backers including Kaszek and Quona. Consumer fintech brand known mostly through online advertising and partnerships in Brazil, with a modest brand profile.

Jordanian commercial bank founded in 1955, offering retail, corporate, SME, investment and treasury banking through a network of branches in Jordan, Palestine and Cyprus. Jordan Ahli Bank is listed on the Amman Stock Exchange (AHLI), headquartered in Amman, and has assets of several billion dollars. Customers are individuals, businesses and institutions, and revenue comes from lending margins, fees and treasury activity. It is among the longer-established Jordanian banks, with high consumer recognition within Jordan but little exposure beyond the region.

Water utility concession serving the western part of Metro Manila, the Philippines, supplying drinking water and wastewater services to millions of residents and businesses in Manila and surrounding cities. Maynilad took over the West Zone concession in 1997, was later controlled by DMCI Holdings and Metro Pacific Investments, and is regulated by the MWSS. Revenue comes from water tariffs, and it has invested in treatment plants and sewerage. Based in Quezon City. Well known to Manila households as a utility, but not a choosing-brand consumer product, with a generally low-profile sponsor history.

Statutory planning and development authority for the Mumbai Metropolitan Region in India, set up in 1975 to plan and fund infrastructure including metro lines, expressways, the Mumbai Trans Harbour Link, flyovers and the Bandra Kurla Complex business district. A government agency under Maharashtra state, it raises money through land sales, bonds, loans and government grants and builds projects for the public. Based in Mumbai. It is a public body with substantial local visibility because of its transport projects, but it does not sell consumer products.

Singapore-based broadband and telecom company founded in 2011 that offers fibre internet, mobile and related services to consumers and businesses in Singapore and, historically, New Zealand and Australia, offering low-priced gigabit plans. Its parent is MyRepublic Group, with investors including Singtel-linked backers and Sunrise Group, and it also operates a Southeast Asia wireless unit. Consumers pay monthly subscriptions and it is also an ISP wholesaler. Known for challenger pricing. Moderate consumer brand awareness in Singapore, and a track record of sports and esports marketing activity.

Large casino hotel on the Atlantic City boardwalk in New Jersey, which opened in 2012 as Revel and was reopened as Ocean Casino Resort in 2018 after bankruptcy. It has about 1,400 hotel rooms, a casino with slots and table games, an online sportsbook and iGaming offered under the Ocean brand, restaurants, nightclubs, a spa and concert venues. Privately owned and led by Bruce Deifik's ownership group. Earns revenue from gaming, hotel stays, dining and entertainment. Strong consumer visibility in the US Northeast and an established local sponsor of sports and events.

Pearl Properties is a real estate company based in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, described as a full-service real estate firm. Crunchbase tags it under construction and consulting, which suggests services spanning development, construction, property management and advisory. It likely serves property owners, tenants and investors in the Philadelphia region. No more detail on size, portfolio or ownership is available. As a regional firm it probably has limited consumer brand awareness outside its home market. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Accounts-payable automation platform for restaurants and hospitality groups that uses OCR and machine learning to capture invoice data, route approvals, and sync with accounting and inventory software. Restaurants subscribe to reduce manual bookkeeping and pay suppliers. Based in San Francisco and founded in 2014, it grew by serving multi-unit operators and food-service groups, and was acquired by Bill.com (now Bill Holdings) in 2022. It was backed by venture funds before the sale. B2B restaurant tech with little consumer awareness, though known among restaurant finance teams.

The Bromley Companies is a New York-based firm in commercial real estate, described as dealing with property management and related real estate services. The data provided does not give more on its portfolio, clients or scale, but the tags suggest property management, leasing and advisory work for owners of commercial property. It is private and B2B, with no evident consumer brand profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

One of the world's largest lessors of intermodal containers, owning a fleet of several million twenty-foot equivalent units of dry, refrigerated, tank and special containers that it leases to shipping lines such as MSC, Maersk and CMA CGM. Revenue comes from leasing and selling containers. Headquartered in Hamilton, Bermuda, with operations in the US and Asia, it was listed on the NYSE (TRTN) from 2016. Brookfield Infrastructure acquired it in 2023 for about 4.7 billion dollars and took it private. Pure B2B with no consumer awareness, but a major logistics-industry name.

Berlin-based SaaS company founded in 2013 whose platform helps brands with many locations manage their online presence, listings, reviews, local search results and customer messaging across Google, Facebook, Apple Maps and other directories. Customers include multi-location chains such as automotive, retail, hospitality and banking brands in Europe and the US. Revenue comes from subscriptions. Uberall has raised venture funding, employs several hundred people and has offices in Germany, the US and elsewhere. B2B, known mainly to marketers rather than consumers.

Video++ is a Shanghai-based company that provides video-streaming services, according to its Crunchbase description, and is tagged under media and entertainment. It likely offers video platform or streaming technology to Chinese media and enterprise customers, but the data given does not confirm products, customers, ownership or size. Little is known about its public brand profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

US real estate investment trust that owns and leases net-leased office and industrial properties to tenants, with a portfolio of roughly 100 properties across about 25 states, and focus on secondary markets. Managed externally by Gladstone Management, part of the Gladstone family of funds founded by David Gladstone, it pays monthly dividends to shareholders and earns rent. Headquartered in McLean, Virginia, it is listed on Nasdaq (GOOD). Customers are corporate tenants, not consumers. Known to income investors, with low general public awareness.

Mazzotta Rentals is a construction rental and sales company based in Middletown, Connecticut. It rents and sells equipment and tools for construction and real estate related work, serving contractors and homeowners in its local area. No further detail on fleet size, staff, ownership or number of branches is available in the data provided. As a regional rental dealer it likely has local brand recognition only. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Multilateral development bank established in 1994 by the Black Sea Economic Cooperation member states, headquartered in Thessaloniki, Greece, and operating since 1999. It lends to and invests in companies and projects in its 11 member countries, including Greece, Turkey, Ukraine, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Albania, Bulgaria, Moldova, Romania and Russia, funding trade, infrastructure, banking and energy. Its capital comes from member governments and it is rated investment grade. B2B and public-sector oriented, with minimal consumer awareness.

Drinks manufacturer, marketer and distributor with a portfolio of cider and beer brands including Bulmers (in Ireland), Magners, Tennent's lager and Menabrea, plus an on-trade distribution arm serving pubs, restaurants and hotels across the UK and Ireland. Revenue comes from alcohol sales and wholesale distribution, with annual sales well over one billion euros. Headquartered in Glasgow with roots in Ireland, it is listed in Dublin and London (CCR). Customers are pubs, retailers and consumers; brand visibility is high in Britain and Ireland, with a long history of sport and festival sponsorship.

Cibuk 2 is a wind energy project company based in Novi Beograd, Serbia. Its Crunchbase tag lists wind energy, and its description mentions supporting local community initiatives around the project. It most likely owns and operates a wind farm that sells electricity into the Serbian grid, but the data provided does not specify capacity, owners or financing. Being a project vehicle, it has no consumer brand and customers are the grid operator and utilities. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Zambian power company that transmits, distributes and supplies electricity, mainly to the copper mines of the Copperbelt and North-Western provinces, and also sells power to other utilities across the region through interconnectors. It also has a telecom and fibre arm and runs solar and thermal generation projects. Based in Kitwe, it is listed on the Lusaka Securities Exchange (CEC), with Zambian institutional investors among its shareholders. Customers are mainly large mining companies, making it B2B with little consumer profile and a low public brand presence outside Zambia's industrial sector.

US health benefits company that sells employer-based health plans, built around self-funded plans and virtual primary care, and a related testing business that rose during the COVID-19 pandemic. Curative, based in Austin, Texas, was founded by Fred Turner and ran drive-through COVID tests, then moved into insurance plans for small and mid-sized employers, with a focus on lower out-of-pocket costs for members. It raised substantial venture funding, including a large 2021 round. Customers are employers and their staff. Moderate awareness among HR buyers and COVID test users in the US.

Cloud-based internet security company that provided email security, web security and threat intelligence to service providers and enterprises, built on data from billions of daily transactions. Founded as Commtouch in Israel, it was renamed Cyren and moved its headquarters to McLean, Virginia, while keeping research operations in Israel and Germany. It was listed on Nasdaq (CYRN) and its customers included Microsoft, Google and security vendors who embedded its threat feeds. It entered insolvency in 2022 and its assets were acquired by Data443. B2B, with limited consumer awareness.

US consumer lender offering fast online loans secured against the equity in a customer's car, aimed at borrowers with limited access to traditional credit. Based in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, it earns interest and fees on loans held against vehicle titles in the states where it operates. Customers are individual consumers with urgent cash needs. It has raised debt and equity financing to fund its lending. Brand visibility is limited and mostly through online advertising to subprime borrowers, not a mass-market name.

Boutique indoor cycling fitness studio chain, founded in 2010 in New York with its signature Torqboard scoring system, that offered group stadium-style rides, a premium boutique experience and later an at-home bike and streaming service. It had around 40 studios across the US, with HQ in Austin, Texas in later years, and earned money from class packs, memberships and merchandise. Flywheel closed its studios in 2020 during the pandemic, and Peloton acquired its intellectual property after a patent dispute. Had good consumer visibility among urban fitness consumers, but no longer operates as a business.

Large Hollywood talent and literary agency representing actors, directors, writers, authors, musicians, athletes and creators, and packaging film, television and book deals. Formed in 2012 when ICM's partners bought out the agency and rebranded it ICM Partners, with offices in Los Angeles, New York, London and elsewhere, it earns commissions of roughly ten percent on clients' earnings. Its clients have included major film and television names. The firm has also had a sports and esports practice. B2B with high industry recognition and strong access to celebrity talent, but little consumer profile.

Restaurant technology platform that consolidated orders from delivery apps such as Uber Eats, DoorDash and Grubhub onto a single tablet and printer, and helped restaurants run virtual brands through delivery-only kitchens. Founded in 2016 in Los Angeles, it charged restaurants software fees and commissions on orders. Customers were restaurant owners and chains. Grubhub acquired Ordermark in 2021 to strengthen its restaurant tools, and it now sits within Grubhub (itself owned by Wonder from 2025). B2B with limited public brand awareness.

French quantum computing company building quantum processors based on neutral atoms trapped by laser tweezers, and offering them via cloud and on-premise systems for research and industry. Spun out in 2019 from the Institut d'Optique in Palaiseau and founded by Nobel physicist Alain Aspect and others, it has raised over 100 million euros including a 2023 round of more than 100 million euros. Customers include supercomputing centres, energy and finance firms, and it has partnerships with GENCI and the European HPC programme. B2B deep tech with high visibility in quantum circles but low consumer awareness.

Wellness franchise operator offering cryotherapy, infrared sauna, red light therapy, IV drips, compression therapy and other recovery services under the Restore Hyper Wellness brand. Founded in 2015 in Austin, Texas, it sells memberships and sessions to health-conscious consumers, athletes and recovery seekers through more than 200 franchise locations in the US and Canada, mainly in affluent suburbs. Backed by venture and private equity investors, it earns franchise fees, royalties and company-owned studio sales. Growing consumer brand with retail footprint, and natural fit with sport-related partnerships.

SDRE Homebuyers is a real estate investment firm based in San Diego, California, according to its Crunchbase profile, and it is tagged under property development. Firms of this kind typically buy houses directly from owners for cash and renovate or resell them, but the data given does not confirm its exact model, size or ownership. It is a local, consumer-facing business that likely markets to homeowners wanting a quick sale. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

French fabless semiconductor company designing high-performance, energy-efficient microprocessors for European supercomputers and AI, led by its Rhea CPU family based on Arm Neoverse cores. Founded in 2019 in Maisons-Laffitte near Paris by Philippe Notton, it was chosen as the processor supplier for Europe's first exascale supercomputer, JUPITER, through the European Processor Initiative. Funding has come from the European Union, French state, and investors such as Arm, Eurazeo and Cathay Capital. Customers are HPC centres and server makers. B2B deep-tech company, a source of European tech sovereignty pride but with low consumer awareness.

Commercial real estate finance company, structured as a REIT, that originates short-term first mortgage loans on transitional commercial properties, particularly in the US South and Southeast. It was spun off from AFC Gamma, the cannabis lender, in 2024 and listed on Nasdaq (SUNS). It is externally managed by an affiliate of the former Chicago Atlantic/AFC group, and earns net interest income from its loan book. Based in West Palm Beach, Florida. Investor-facing and B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

Chinese record label and music group formed from Alibaba's music assets, including Xiami Music and Alibaba's licensed library, renamed Taihe Music Group in 2021. It signs artists, owns and licenses music rights, publishes songs, and runs services such as the Taihe Music app and live-event and talent platforms. Revenue comes from licensing, streaming, and artist management. Based in Beijing and tied to Alibaba Group's entertainment arm, it works with Chinese streaming platforms and brands. Moderate brand profile in the Chinese music industry, with little recognition abroad.

UK property development arm of YTL Corporation, the Malaysian conglomerate, active in residential and commercial development in the Bristol area, notably the Brabazon scheme on the former Filton Airfield, which aims to include thousands of homes, a campus, a Bristol arena, and a rail station. Revenue comes from land sale, building and leasing, and the group also owns YTL Arena Bristol. Based in Bristol, it belongs to the wider YTL group, which also owns Wessex Water and hotels. Brand visibility is regional and rising through the arena venue.

US specialty insurance group writing excess and surplus lines coverage, aimed at small and mid-sized businesses through wholesale brokers, with a technology-driven underwriting approach.
